facts.text: The applicant was born in 1952 and lives in Ankara. He is a lawyer and a former member of the Turkish Grand National Assembly.

anchor.surface_text: 9.  The applicant was born in 1952 and lives in Ankara. He is a lawyer and a former member of the Turkish Grand National Assembly.

facts.text: The applicant wrote a novel entitled “The Heat of Şiro” (Şiro'nun Ateşi). The book was based on real events which took place in Ormaniçi village in the province of Şırnak. The book was published in September 1997 by the Berfin Publishing Company.

anchor.surface_text: 10.  The applicant wrote a novel entitled “The Heat of Şiro” (Şiro'nun Ateşi). The book was based on real events which took place in Ormaniçi village in the province of Şırnak. The book was published in September 1997 by the Berfin Publishing Company.

facts.text: On 14 October 1997 the public prosecutor at the Istanbul State Security Court requested the seizure of copies of the book, contending that the content incited hatred and hostility by making distinctions between Turkish citizens based on ethnic or regional identity.

anchor.surface_text: 11.  On 14 October 1997 the public prosecutor at the Istanbul State Security Court requested the seizure of copies of the book. The public prosecutor contended that the content of the book incited hatred and hostility by making distinctions between Turkish citizens based on grounds of their ethnic or regional identity.

facts.text: On 14 October 1997 a single judge of the State Security Court accepted the public prosecutor's submissions and made an interim order for the seizure of copies of the first edition of the book, holding that it incited hatred and hostility and was not protected artistic expression.

anchor.surface_text: 12.  On 14 October 1997 a single judge of the State Security Court accepted the submissions of the public prosecutor and made an interim order for the seizure of copies of the first edition of the book. In its decision (no. 1997/442), the State Security Court held that the book, by attributing extremely disgusting acts to the security forces, identified with names and rank, incited people to hatred and hostility by making distinctions between Turkish citizens based on grounds of their ethnic or regional identity. The court further held that, while artistic expression fell within freedom of expression, that freedom was not absolute and that the dissemination of distasteful and disgusting texts by way of a novel could not be considered to be artistic expression.

facts.text: According to the applicant, copies were seized, but the seizure protocol drafted by the police and signed by the owner of the publishing company on 15 October 1997 recorded that copies of the book were not found.

anchor.surface_text: 13.  According to the applicant, copies were then seized. However, the seizure protocol drafted by the police and signed by the owner of the publishing company on 15 October 1997 recorded that copies of the book were not found.

facts.text: The Government highlighted passages on pages 202 and 203 of the book containing violent and hostile language against tyrants and security forces.

anchor.surface_text: 14.  The Government in their observations drew attention to following passages on pages 202 and 203 of the book: “... Ah, I wish I were strong like before so that I could catch Mizrak in the meadow of Bana. Then he would have understood what the world is like. I would have stripped him under the summer sun; I would have had him walk before Kümeyt and whipped him all day long. ...

facts.text: On 20 October 1997 the applicant appealed against the seizure order, alleging unjustified interference with his freedom of expression, but gave an incorrect case number, resulting in the appeal court not considering his case but another relating to a poetry book.

anchor.surface_text: 15.  On 20 October 1997 the applicant appealed against the seizure order. The applicant averred that the seizure order constituted an unjustified interference with his right to freedom of expression guaranteed by the European Convention on Human Rights. However he gave an incorrect case number on his appeal. As a result it appears that the appeal court did not consider the facts of his case, but that of another (relating to a poetry book).

facts.text: On 5 November 1997 the Istanbul State Security Court dismissed the applicant's appeal and upheld the seizure order and the single judge's reasons for issuing it.

anchor.surface_text: On 5 November 1997 the Istanbul State Security Court dismissed the applicant's appeal and upheld the order, together with the single judge's reasons for issuing it.

facts.text: On 21 November 1997 the public prosecutor filed a bill of indictment against the applicant and requested conviction and sentencing under the Prevention of Terrorism Act 1991.

anchor.surface_text: 16.  On 21 November 1997 the public prosecutor attached to the Istanbul State Security Court filed a bill of indictment against the applicant and requested that he be convicted and sentenced under the Prevention of Terrorism Act 1991.

facts.text: During a hearing on 18 February 1998 before the Istanbul State Security Court, the applicant requested annulment of the interim seizure order; the matter was adjourned to 15 April 1998.

anchor.surface_text: 17.  During a hearing held on 18 February 1998 before the Istanbul State Security Court, the applicant requested the court to annul the interim seizure order against his book. The matter was adjourned to the next hearing, fixed for 15 April 1998.

facts.text: On 2 September 1999 Law No. 4454 concerning suspension of pending cases and penalties in media-related offences entered into force.

anchor.surface_text: 18.   On 2 September 1999 Law No. 4454 concerning the suspension of pending cases and penalties in media-related offences entered into force.

facts.text: On 24 September 1999 the Istanbul State Security Court suspended the proceedings against the applicant but did not decide on his request to annul the interim seizure order against his book.

anchor.surface_text: 19.  On 24 September 1999 the Istanbul State Security Court suspended the proceedings brought against the applicant. The court, however, did not determine the applicant's request to annul the interim seizure order against his book.

He submitted that the domestic courts decided on the interim seizure order without carefully reading his book. In this connection, he pointed out that, had the authorities read it carefully, they would have seen that the book contained fictional characters of different ethnic origin and that there was no reference to the names or rank of the security forces who had actually taken part in the events in Ormani�e7i. Consequently, the applicant considered that the interference with his right to freedom of expression was not necessary in a democratic society.
